### sts-assumerolewithsaml-duration

**Scope.** per AssumeRoleWithSAML call; default; adjustable; whichever is shorter: DurationSeconds or the SAML SessionNotOnOrAfter value.

> "By default, the temporary security credentials created by `AssumeRoleWithSAML` last for one hour. Your role session lasts for the duration that you specify, or until the time specified in the SAML authentication response's `SessionNotOnOrAfter` value, whichever is shorter. You can provide a `DurationSeconds` value from 900 seconds (15 minutes) up to the maximum session duration setting for the role."

### sts-request-quota-600-rps

**Claim.** For AWS STS requests made using AWS credentials, the default request quota is 600 requests per second, per account, per Region; requests by AWS service principals do not consume it, and for a cross-account AssumeRole only the account making the request has its quota consumed.

**Write it as.** `600 requests per second`

**Scope.** per account, per Region; default; adjustable; requests made using AWS credentials; service principals do not consume it.

> "For AWS STS requests made using AWS credentials, the default request quota is 600 requests per second, per account, per Region."
> — [IAM and AWS STS quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_iam-quotas.html)

> "Requests to AWS STS by AWS service principals, such as those used to assume roles for use with an AWS service, do not consume STS request per second quota in your accounts."
> — [IAM and AWS STS quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_iam-quotas.html)

> "For cross-account AssumeRole requests, only the account making the AssumeRole request impacts the STS quota. The target account does not have any of it’s quota consumed."
> — [IAM and AWS STS quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_iam-quotas.html)

> "To request an increase to STS request quotas, please open a ticket with AWS support."
> — [IAM and AWS STS quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_iam-quotas.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### sts-role-chaining-definition

**Claim.** Role chaining is using a role to assume a second role; it can be done by switching roles in the console, with the CLI or with the API, and transitive session tags are passed to every later session in the chain.

**Write it as.** `use a role to assume a second role` · `transitive session tags are passed to all subsequent sessions in a role chain`

> "Role chaining is when you use a role to assume a second role. You can perform role chaining through the AWS Management Console by switching roles, the AWS CLI, or API."
> — [IAM roles](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles.html)

> "When you assume a role, you can pass a session tag and set the tag as transitive. Transitive session tags are passed to all subsequent sessions in a role chain."
> — [IAM roles](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-11.

### sts-role-chaining-max-one-hour

**Claim.** Role chaining (using one role's credentials to assume a second role) limits the session to a maximum of one hour regardless of the roles' maximum session duration settings; a DurationSeconds above one hour makes the operation fail.

**Write it as.** `one hour` · `the operation fails`

**Scope.** per role session obtained through role chaining; maximum; applies regardless of the maximum session duration configured for individual roles.

> "Role chaining limits your AWS Management Console, AWS CLI or AWS API role session to a maximum of one hour. It applies regardless of the maximum session duration configured for individual roles."
> — [IAM roles](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles.html)

> "However, if you assume a role using role chaining and provide a `DurationSeconds` parameter value greater than one hour, the operation fails."
> — [AssumeRole](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/STS/latest/APIReference/API_AssumeRole.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-11.

### sts-saml-and-web-identity-callers-no-mfa

**Claim.** AssumeRoleWithSAML and AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity can be called by any user who presents a SAML authentication response or an OIDC-compliant JWT from a known identity provider; both are unsigned calls, not signed with AWS credentials, and the calls do not support MFA because the user is authenticated by an external provider.

**Write it as.** `any user who presents a SAML authentication response or an OIDC-compliant JWT` · `not signed with AWS credentials` · `do not support MFA`

**Scope.** AssumeRoleWithSAML and AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity.

> "AssumeRoleWithSAML | Any user; caller must pass a SAML authentication response that indicates authentication from a known identity provider | 15 m \| Maximum session duration setting³ \| 1 hr | No | Yes | Cannot call `GetFederationToken` or `GetSessionToken`." (columns: **AWS STS API** | **Who can call** | **Credential lifetime (min \| max \| default)** | **MFA support**¹ | **Session policy support**² | **Restrictions on resulting temporary credentials**)
> — [Compare AWS STS credentials](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_sts-comparison.html)

> "AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity | Any user; caller must pass an OIDC compliant JWT token that indicates authentication from a known identity provider | 15 m \| Maximum session duration setting³ \| 1 hr | No | Yes | Cannot call `GetFederationToken` or `GetSessionToken`." (columns: **AWS STS API** | **Who can call** | **Credential lifetime (min \| max \| default)** | **MFA support**¹ | **Session policy support**² | **Restrictions on resulting temporary credentials**)
> — [Compare AWS STS credentials](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_sts-comparison.html)

> "`AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` requests are not signed with, and do not require AWS credentials."
> — [Request temporary security credentials](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_temp_request.html)

> "This is an unsigned call, meaning you do not need to authenticate AWS security credentials prior to making the request."
> — [Request temporary security credentials](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_temp_request.html)

> "For `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` and `AssumeRoleWithSAML`, the user is authenticated by an external provider and AWS cannot determine whether that provider required MFA."
> — [Secure API access with MFA](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_mfa_configure-api-require.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### sts-service-principal-requests-do-not-consume-quota

**Claim.** STS requests made by AWS service principals, such as a service assuming a role for its own use, do not consume the account's STS requests per second quota.

**Write it as.** `do not consume STS request per second quota`

**Scope.** per account, per Region; fixed; not adjustable; requests by AWS service principals.

> "Requests to AWS STS by AWS service principals, such as those used to assume roles for use with an AWS service, do not consume STS request per second quota in your accounts."
> — [IAM and AWS STS quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_iam-quotas.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### sts-session-policy-intersection

**Claim.** A session's permissions are the intersection of the identity-based policies of the user or role that created the session and the session policies, and permissions can also come from a resource-based policy; a session policy cannot grant more permissions than the identity-based policy of the role being assumed allows, and an explicit deny in any of these policies overrides the allow.

**Write it as.** `the intersection of the identity-based policies` · `An explicit deny in any of these policies overrides the allow`

**Scope.** per role session.

> "The permissions for a session are the intersection of the identity-based policies for the IAM entity (user or role) used to create the session and the session policies. Permissions can also come from a resource-based policy. An explicit deny in any of these policies overrides the allow."
> — [Policies and permissions in AWS Identity and Access Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies.html)

> "You cannot use session policies to grant more permissions than those allowed by the identity-based policy of the role that is being assumed."
> — [AssumeRole](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/STS/latest/APIReference/API_AssumeRole.html)

> "You cannot use session policies to grant more permissions than those allowed by the identity-based policy of the role that is being assumed."
> — [AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/STS/latest/APIReference/API_AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### sts-session-policy-limits

**Claim.** An AssumeRole, AssumeRoleWithSAML or AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity call can pass one inline JSON session policy and up to 10 managed policy ARNs, and the plaintext of inline and managed session policies together cannot exceed 2,048 characters.

**Write it as.** `up to 10 managed policy` · `2,048 characters`

**Scope.** per AssumeRole, AssumeRoleWithSAML or AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity request; maximum; not adjustable; inline and managed session policies combined.

> "You can pass a single JSON policy document to use as an inline session policy. You can also specify up to 10 managed policy Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) to use as managed session policies. The plaintext that you use for both inline and managed session policies can't exceed 2,048 characters."
> — [AssumeRole](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/STS/latest/APIReference/API_AssumeRole.html)

> "You can pass a single JSON policy document to use as an inline session policy. You can also specify up to 10 managed policy Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) to use as managed session policies. The plaintext that you use for both inline and managed session policies can't exceed 2,048 characters."
> — [AssumeRoleWithSAML](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/STS/latest/APIReference/API_AssumeRoleWithSAML.html)

> "You can pass a single JSON policy document to use as an inline session policy. You can also specify up to 10 managed policy Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) to use as managed session policies. The plaintext that you use for both inline and managed session policies can't exceed 2,048 characters."
> — [AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/STS/latest/APIReference/API_AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity.html)

> "You can pass a single JSON inline session policy document using the `Policy` parameter. You can use the `PolicyArns` parameter to specify up to 10 managed session policies."
> — [Policies and permissions in AWS Identity and Access Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### sts-session-tags-transitive-for-role-chaining

**Claim.** Session tags are key-value attributes passed when you assume a role or federate a user; they are valid only for the current session, and by default STS does not pass them to later role sessions unless you set them as transitive, which persist during role chaining.

**Write it as.** `valid only for the current session` · `unless you set them as transitive`

**Scope.** AWS STS session tags; default; role chaining.

> "Session tags are key-value pair attributes that you pass when you assume an IAM role or federate a user in AWS STS."
> — [Pass session tags in AWS STS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_session-tags.html)

> "Session tags are valid only for the current session."
> — [Pass session tags in AWS STS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_session-tags.html)

> "By default, AWS STS does not pass tags to subsequent role sessions. However, you can set session tags as transitive. Transitive tags persist during role chaining and replace matching `ResourceTag` values after the evaluation of the role trust policy."
> — [Pass session tags in AWS STS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_session-tags.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### sts-source-identity-persists-and-cannot-change

**Claim.** A source identity is a custom string that identifies the person or application using a role, and it is stored as the source identity in AWS CloudTrail; once set, it is present in requests for any AWS action taken during the role session, it persists when a role is used to assume another role through the AWS CLI or AWS API (role chaining), and it cannot be changed during the role session. AWS recommends it to control the identity that assumes a role and to find in CloudTrail who used the role.

**Write it as.** `persists when a role is used to assume another role` · `cannot be changed during the role session`

**Scope.** AWS STS source identity.

> "After a source identity is set, it is present in requests for any AWS action taken during the role session. The value that is set persists when a role is used to assume another role through the AWS CLI or AWS API, known as role chaining. The value that is set cannot be changed during the role session."
> — [Monitor and control actions taken with assumed roles](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_temp_control-access_monitor.html)

> "Administrators can configure roles to require identities to pass a custom string that identifies the person or application that is performing actions in AWS. This identity information is stored as the source identity in AWS CloudTrail."
> — [Monitor and control actions taken with assumed roles](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_temp_control-access_monitor.html)

> "We recommend that you use source identity when you want to control the identity that assumes a role. Source identity is also useful for mining CloudTrail logs to determine who used the role to perform actions."
> — [Monitor and control actions taken with assumed roles](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_temp_control-access_monitor.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### sts-temporary-credentials-advantages

**Claim.** Temporary credentials mean you do not have to distribute or embed long-term credentials in an application, you can give users access to your AWS resources without defining an AWS identity for them, and you do not have to update or revoke them because they expire (they have a limited lifetime); they are the basis for roles and identity federation.

**Write it as.** `do not have to distribute or embed long-term credentials in an application` · `the basis for roles and identity federation` · `do not have to update or revoke them because they expire`

**Scope.** AWS STS credentials.

> "You do not have to distribute or embed long-term AWS security credentials with an application."
> — [Temporary security credentials in IAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_temp.html)

> "You can provide access to your AWS resources to users without having to define an AWS identity for them. Temporary credentials are the basis for roles and identity federation."
> — [Temporary security credentials in IAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_temp.html)

> "The temporary security credentials have a limited lifetime, so you do not have to update them or explicitly revoke them when they're no longer needed."
> — [Temporary security credentials in IAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_temp.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### sts-temporary-credentials-cannot-be-reused-after-expiry

Replaced by [sts-temporary-credentials-expire-not-stored](#sts-temporary-credentials-expire-not-stored).

### sts-temporary-credentials-cannot-be-revoked-permissions-can-change

**Claim.** Temporary security credentials stay valid until they expire and cannot be revoked, but their permissions are evaluated on every request, so changing their access rights has the effect of revoking them.

**Write it as.** `cannot be revoked` · `evaluated each time a request is made`

**Scope.** temporary security credentials issued by AWS STS.

> "After AWS STS issues temporary security credentials, they are valid through the expiration period and cannot be revoked. However, the permissions assigned to temporary security credentials are evaluated each time a request is made that uses the credentials, so you can achieve the effect of revoking the credentials by changing their access rights after they have been issued."
> — [Permissions for temporary security credentials](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_temp_control-access.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### sts-temporary-credentials-expire-not-stored

**Claim.** Temporary security credentials are short-term and generated dynamically on request rather than stored with the user; after they expire AWS no longer accepts any API request made with them, and they cannot be reused.

**Write it as.** `generated dynamically on request rather than stored with the user` · `after they expire AWS no longer accepts any API request made with them` · `they cannot be reused` · `generated dynamically and provided to the user`

**Scope.** every AWS STS credential.

> "After the credentials expire, AWS no longer recognizes them or allows any kind of access from API requests made with them."
> — [Temporary security credentials in IAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_temp.html)

> "Temporary security credentials are not stored with the user but are generated dynamically and provided to the user when requested."
> — [Temporary security credentials in IAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_temp.html)

> "After temporary security credentials expire, they cannot be reused. You can specify how long the credentials are valid, up to a maximum limit."
> — [Temporary security credentials in IAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_temp.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-11.

### sts-temporary-credentials-include-session-token

**Claim.** A set of temporary security credentials is an access key ID, a secret access key and a session token; every call made with them must include the session token, and they cannot be extended or refreshed beyond their original interval.

**Write it as.** `an access key ID, a secret access key and a session token` · `every call made with them must include the session token` · `cannot be extended or refreshed beyond their original interval`

**Scope.** every AWS STS credential.

> "The AWS STS API operations create a new session with temporary security credentials that include an access key pair and a session token. The access key pair consists of an access key ID and a secret key."
> — [Request temporary security credentials](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_temp_request.html)

> "Temporary credentials cannot be extended or refreshed beyond the original specified interval."
> — [Use temporary credentials with AWS resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_temp_use-resources.html)

> "When you make a call using temporary security credentials, the call must include a session token, which is returned along with those temporary credentials. AWS uses the session token to validate the temporary security credentials."
> — [Use temporary credentials with AWS resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_temp_use-resources.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-11.

### sts-vpc-endpoint-policy-default-and-no-grant

**Claim.** An endpoint policy on an STS interface VPC endpoint controls which principals can use it and which STS actions; without a policy the default allows all STS actions for all principals, and endpoint policies never grant permissions on their own, so both the endpoint policy and the caller's policies must allow the request.

**Write it as.** `the default allows all STS actions for all principals` · `both the endpoint policy and the caller's policies must allow the request`

**Scope.** AWS STS interface VPC endpoint policies; default.

> "The policy controls which principals can use the endpoint and which AWS STS actions they can perform. If you don't attach a policy, the endpoint uses the default policy that allows unrestricted access to all AWS STS actions for all principals."
> — [Control access to AWS STS with VPC endpoint policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_sts_vpc_endpoint_policies.html)

> "VPC endpoint policies don't grant permissions on their own. They act as an additional boundary that works alongside other policies. Both the endpoint policy and the caller's applicable policies must allow a request for it to succeed."
> — [Control access to AWS STS with VPC endpoint policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_sts_vpc_endpoint_policies.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.
